messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 GPU OOM detected on node gpu-prod-42 (us-west2). Summary: container redwood-runtime-7 crashed during generation loop. Node reports ~6.2GB free headroom in allocator but CUDA OOM triggered. Auto-restart initiated.

maria-oncall: acked. I'm looking. Any immediate customer alerts? @anya-cs can you check impacted customers and hold off comms until we know whether fallback triggered? :point_up:

josh-rt: grabbing logs from the node now. Spawning `kubectl logs` and `nvidia-smi` snapshot.

sam-mlinfra: past incidents have shown fragmentation + reserved blocks mismatch. Can you paste the allocator snapshot (`/var/log/alloc-metrics.json`)?

maria-oncall: pasting trimmed logs below (timestamps omitted):
```
[alloc] total_gpu=40GB free_reported=6.2GB reserved_total=8GB reserved_available=2.1GB
[kv-cache] pinned=1.6GB prefix_cache=3.4GB evictable=0.0GB
[cuda] cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources at kernel.cu:234
[container] runtime exit code=137 OOM
[telemetry] contiguous_free_max=80MB fragmentation_ratio=0.82
```

josh-rt: interesting — allocator reports 6.2GB free overall, but contiguous_free_max is only 80MB. That matches fragmentation. Also reserved_available 2.1GB but kv-cache pinned almost all of it.

lee-sre: can we confirm whether prefetch path recently changed? The prefetcher has a habit of temporarily inflating ephemeral allocations that don't show in reserved accounting.

sam-mlinfra: yes, we rolled a prefetch tweak to parallelize 4->8 prefetch workers earlier today (rollout at 08:12 PDT). I suspect transient bursts allocate many small pinned buffers that leave holes between big allocations.

maria-oncall: action plan: 1) prevent further container restarts; 2) free kv-cache and reduce reserved pool temporarily; 3) migrate active sessions off node if necessary; 4) update incident timeline. I'm going to cordon gpu-prod-42 and scale down pod to 0 to let other nodes pick up traffic.

josh-rt: commands I ran:
```
kubectl cordon node/gpu-prod-42
kubectl scale deployment redwood-runtime --replicas=0 -n inference --selector=pod=redwood-runtime-7
nvtop snapshot -> attached to thread
```

maria-oncall: cordon done. scaling down runtime pods now.

anya-cs: quick customer update: two customers saw failing requests for ~3 minutes (no data loss, just elevated 5xx). I've queued an inbound support note; will hold public status until we confirm root cause.

sam-mlinfra: I ran `alloc-dump` (attached) — allocator slab sizes show heavy utilization of 256MB and 1MB buckets, but contiguous runs show lots of 32KB holes. Looks like fragmentation from many small allocations interleaved with occasional big KV allocations. Also saw `reserve_count` accounting mismatch: reserved_total=8GB but sum(reserved_blocks) ~7.1GB in the allocator map — something holding ~900MB in an ephemeral pool not surfaced.

lee-sre: ephemeral pool could be the new prefetch work queue. The code path used a temporary pinned buffer per worker; at 8 workers that's ~128MB * 8 = ~1GB. If they don't release quickly under pressure, that explains the mismatch.

maria-oncall: mitigation steps executed:
- Reduced prefetch workers from 8 -> 2 via runtime flag (applied as emergency config).
- Evicted KV prefix cache on node (runtime admin API: `POST /admin/evict?kv=prefix`).
- Lowered reserved pool soft target by 15% to increase available contiguous space.
- Restarted container after drains.

josh-rt: logs after mitigation show:
```
[alloc] total_gpu=40GB free_reported=8.1GB reserved_total=6.8GB reserved_available=4.7GB
[cuda] no new OOMs in 4 minutes
[telemetry] contiguous_free_max=1.1GB fragmentation_ratio=0.44
```

maria-oncall: good — node stabilized after restart. I'm keeping cordon for 15 minutes to observe.

anya-cs: customer-impact summary for postmortem: two accounts experienced 5xx for ~3 minutes. One is on dedicated capacity (reported latency spikes, no data exfiltration). CS will reach out with targeted message once we have RCA.

sam-mlinfra: preliminary root cause hypothesis: combined effect of (A) prefetch worker increase causing ephemeral pinned buffers that are not accounted in reserved_total, (B) allocator fragmentation (many small allocations left interleaved with KV large buffers) leading to low contiguous_max, (C) reserved blocks rounding + soft-reserve heuristic that allowed kernel launch needing contiguous >80MB to fail. The system-level headroom metric was correct in aggregate but didn't reflect fragmentation and hidden ephemeral retention.

lee-sre: short-term mitigations to push cluster-wide:
- Revert prefetch worker change (rollback flag in config).
- Add emergency eviction hook for prefix KV to run when contiguous_free_max < 200MB.
- Lower default reserved pool by 10% for the next 24h.

maria-oncall: I'm scheduling an emergency patch: adjust headroom calc to expose ephemeral pools (add ephemeral_track flag to allocator) and change allocation fallback to trigger early eviction if contiguous_free_max < required_contig * 1.2. Also we should add an alert that triggers on contiguous_free_max dropping under 300MB even if aggregate free > 2GB.

sam-mlinfra: I'll open PR with the allocator change and a short-circuit to reduce prefetch workers on startup if fragmentation ratio > 0.6. Tagging @josh-rt for review.

josh-rt: reviewing now. Also recommend we instrument per-worker pinned buffer accounting so telemetry shows ephemeral retention in the next deploy.

maria-oncall: timeline so far:
- 08:12 rollout: prefetch workers 4 -> 8 (canary)
- 08:47 multiple crashes start, incident-bot triggers at 08:49 (2399990000)
- 08:50 node cordoned and pods scaled down
- 08:53 KV evicted and prefetch reduced, restarted container
- 08:57 node stable, cordon held until 09:12

anya-cs: noted. I'll prepare a customer-safe blurb: "We experienced elevated errors caused by GPU memory fragmentation after a runtime prefetch change. We reverted the change and applied mitigations; affected requests were retried automatically. No customer data was lost." Will send after we finalize RCA.

lee-sre: follow-ups (owner tags):
- sam-mlinfra: allocator telemetry patch + PR (owner)
- josh-rt: review + test PR (owner)
- maria-oncall: incident writeup and postmortem meeting invite (owner)
- anya-cs: customer comms draft (owner)

maria-oncall: thanks all. Leaving node cordoned until patch PR merges to canary. Filing incident ticket: INC-2399990. Will add logs and alloc-dump attachments to ticket. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2399990 created and linked to on-call timeline.

maria-oncall: postmortem notes to include: exact allocator accounting bug, quantification of fragmentation impact, telemetry gaps (ephemeral not tracked), rollback decision timeline, customer impact and support outreach, and long-term mitigations (allocator fix, telemetry, prefetch rate-limiting). Meeting scheduled in 2 hours.

anya-cs: adding draft comms to ticket. Closing thread once PR merges and postmortem posted. :email:

josh-rt: final note — if we see similar spikes, consider temporary cluster-level mitigation: set admission controller to reject new large-sequence requests to nodes with contiguous_free_max < 256MB. That buys time for eviction.

maria-oncall: agreed. Good catch. I'll log that as an action item.
